title: This Lake Gets Hit by Lightning Almost 300 Nights a Year

scenes.text: This lake gets hit by lightning almost 300 nights a year.
Lake Maracaibo, Venezuela. 297 storm nights a year, NASA counted. Up to 28 strikes a minute, ten hours straight.
233 lightning flashes per square kilometre every year. More than anywhere else on Earth.
Warm, wet air rises off the lake at night. Cold mountain winds slam into it, and the sky ignites.
Same storm, same spot, nearly every night of the year.
300 nights a year. Right now, it's probably flashing.

description:
Lake Maracaibo in Venezuela is the lightning capital of the world. NASA satellite data shows about 233 lightning flashes per square kilometre every year and an average of 297 nocturnal thunderstorms a year, peaking in September.
The Catatumbo lightning can fire up to 28 times a minute for up to 10 hours a night, driven by warm moist air rising off the lake and colliding with cold winds from the surrounding mountains.
Would you camp on the shore for one night? Comment below.
first_comment: Before NASA's satellites crowned Lake Maracaibo, the lightning capital was the Congo Basin in Africa. Where is the worst storm you have ever been caught in?
